topics.title: Bobby Vinton Discusses Theater and National Anthem Performance
topics.summary: During a radio broadcast, Bobby Vinton discusses his ambitious plans to open a theater in Missouri, including performing two shows daily. The conversation becomes increasingly bizarre as he recounts an embarrassing experience singing the national anthem due to echo issues at a stadium event, referencing a Polish prince figure and discussing his wife’s fondness for water views before abruptly shifting into a discussion about commercial opportunities and Carl Lewis' performance.

topics.title: Howard Stern's Obsession With Bobby Vinton
topics.summary: During a radio show, Howard Stern discusses his fascination with Bobby Vinton’s unusual songwriting process and preference for wholesome sounds like ‘Blue Velvet.’ He explores how Vinton wrote numerous hits, including 'Roses or Red,' while also detailing the details of recording sessions in Nashville and discussing potential commercial success.

topics.title: Rich Women, Sewing Workers & Stern’s Critique
topics.summary: The broadcast centers on a wealthy woman and the garment workers who create her clothing. The conversation quickly devolves into personal attacks against Howard Stern, critiques of media bias, accusations of dishonesty regarding news reporting, and bizarre tangents about television shows and interview techniques.”” 54 words.

Johnson, Eartha Kitt engaged in an outspoken conversation about the war in Vietnam and expressed her concerns regarding young Americans being sent to fight. The exchange became fraught as she challenged administration policies, leading to nervous reactions from Secret Service personnel due to her direct criticism.
